claim: Sea star oocytes proceed through meiosis with high synchrony (over 90% synchrony of oocytes at germinal vesicle breakdown (GVBD), MI, MII, and pronuclear stages).
source: In an initial trial, we collected oocytes for immunofluorescence every 10 min after 1-MeAd stimulation and determined that oocytes proceed through meiosis with high synchrony (over 90% synchrony of oocytes at germinal vesicle breakdown (GVBD), MI, MII, and pronuclear stages; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunofluorescence time-course experiments and quantification shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: 8026 total proteins were identified in the proteomic analysis.
source: Using MS, we identified 8026 total proteins, of which 6212 were identified in two independent time-course series and 4635 in all three series (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data and is referenced in supplementary files.

claim: 99% of the 4635 proteins reproducibly identified in all three time-course series displayed a maximum fold change of less than 2 from prophase I to the first embryonic cleavage.
source: In fact, 99% of the 4635 proteins reproducibly identified in all three time-course series displayed a maximum fold change of less than 2 from prophase I to the first embryonic cleavage, with 74.8% of proteins displaying less than a 1.2-fold change (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative proteomic data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: 74.8% of proteins displayed less than a 1.2-fold change from prophase I to the first embryonic cleavage.
source: In fact, 99% of the 4635 proteins reproducibly identified in all three time-course series displayed a maximum fold change of less than 2 from prophase I to the first embryonic cleavage, with 74.8% of proteins displaying less than a 1.2-fold change (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative proteomic data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Cyclin B levels are high in prophase I, GVBD, and MI, but decline sharply in MII, before being partially restored in the first cleavage stage.
source: Moreover, cyclin B levels were high in prophase I, GVBD, and MI, but declined sharply in MII, before being partially restored in the first cleavage stage (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Cyclin B dynamics are consistent with Anaphase Promoting Complex/Cyclosome (APC/C) mediated destruction of cyclin B during cell cycle progression.
source: These dynamics are consistent with Anaphase Promoting Complex/Cyclosome (APC/C) mediated destruction of cyclin B during cell cycle progression (Evans et al., 1983; Kishimoto, 2018; Okano-Uchida et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work on APC/C-mediated cyclin B destruction.

claim: PIM-1 is absent in prophase I oocytes but translated de novo following meiotic resumption.
source: In addition, we identified the serine/threonine kinase Proviral integration site for Moloney murine leukemia virus-1 (PIM-1) (Figure 1F), previously proposed to be a potential mitotic regulator (Bachmann et al., 2006), as a protein that is absent in prophase I oocytes but translated de novo following meiotic resumption.
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic data shown in Figure 1F and cited prior work.

claim: Emetine-treated oocytes responded to 1-MeAd stimulation to initiate MI.
source: Emetine-treated oocytes responded to 1-MeAd stimulation to initiate MI, consistent with prior work (Houk and Epel, 1974).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations and cited prior work.

claim: Instead of progressing to MII, emetine-treated oocytes had maternal DNA decondense and form a pronucleus with oocytes remaining arrested.
source: However, instead of progressing to MII, the maternal DNA decondensed and formed a pronucleus with oocytes remaining arrested even at time points when control oocytes had initiated first cleavage (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: Only 108 out of 7610 proteins identified significantly changed with emetine treatment.
source: Based on a proteomic analysis of MII and pronuclear stage oocytes, we found that only 108 out of 7610 proteins identified in our analysis significantly changed with emetine treatment (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, supplementary file 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and supplementary file 3.

claim: Emetine-sensitive proteins were overrepresented for cytoskeletal elements and actomyosin-related proteins.
source: These emetine-sensitive proteins fell into diverse categories but were overrepresented for cytoskeletal elements and actomyosin-related proteins (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene ontology analysis referenced in supplementary file 4.

claim: New protein synthesis is required for progression past MI.
source: In summary, most proteins are insensitive to translational inhibition, indicating a general lack of turnover between MI and MII, but new protein synthesis is required for progression past MI.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from emetine treatment experiments.

claim: Blocking cyclin A synthesis did not affect the meiotic divisions but caused an arrest prior to the first cleavage.
source: When new cyclin A synthesis was blocked, oocytes underwent both meiotic divisions normally and the maternal and paternal pronuclei fused, but these zygotes then arrested with a single fused pronucleus and failed to progress to the first cleavage (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by morpholino knockdown experiments shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: Cyclin A is required for the transition to embryogenesis in P. pectinifera.
source: This is consistent with a role for cyclin A in mitotic entry in cultured cells, and the transition to embryogenesis in P. pectinifera (Hara et al., 2009; Okano-Uchida et al., 2003; Pagano et al., 1992).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Preventing cyclin B synthesis resulted in a normal MI division but failure to extrude the second polar body.
source: In contrast, preventing cyclin B synthesis resulted in a normal MI division but failure to extrude the second polar body and retention of an additional centriole.
evidence: The claim is supported by morpholino knockdown experiments.

claim: Cyclin B must be translated de novo following anaphase I to drive meiosis II but is dispensable for the initial transition from meiosis to embryonic mitosis.
source: This suggests that cyclin B must be translated de novo following anaphase I to drive meiosis II but is dispensable for the initial transition from meiosis to embryonic mitosis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from morpholino knockdown experiments showing cyclin B is required for MII but not first cleavage.

claim: Simultaneously preventing the new translation of both cyclin A and B resulted in oocytes completing MI and then arresting in a pronuclear-like state without conducting MII.
source: Finally, when we simultaneously prevented the new translation of both cyclin A and B, oocytes completed MI and then arrested in a pronuclear-like state without conducting MII (Figure 2C,D), similar to the effect of translational inhibition by emetine (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by morpholino knockdown experiments shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: The proteome during the oocyte-to-embryo transition is highly stable but the de novo translation of cyclins is required for meiotic progression.
source: Taken together, our results suggest that the proteome during the oocyte-to-embryo transition is highly stable but that the de novo translation of cyclins is required for meiotic progression.
evidence: The claim is a summary inference from the proteomic and morpholino experiments.

claim: A total of 25,228 phosphopeptides were identified across three multiplexed time courses.
source: Our analysis identified a total of 25,228 phosphopeptides across three multiplexed time courses.
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic mass spectrometry data.

claim: Among phosphopeptides, 16,691 were identified in two, and 11,430 in three, multiplexes.
source: Among those phosphopeptides, 16,691 were identified in two, and 11,430 in three, multiplexes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, supplementary file 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and supplementary file 5.

claim: 79.3% of phosphorylation was detected on serine residues, 19.6% on threonine, and 1.1% on tyrosine residues based on a phosphorylation localization probability of ≥0.9.
source: We detected 79.3% of phosphorylation on serine residues, 19.6% on threonine, and 1.1% on tyrosine residues based on a phosphorylation localization probability of ≥0.9 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Prior work found similar ratios of S:T:Y phosphorylation based on autoradiographic measurements in chicken cells (92%:7.7%:0.3%) and based on phosphoproteomics in human cells (84.1%:15.5%:0.4%).
source: Prior work found similar ratios of S:T:Y phosphorylation based on autoradiographic measurements in chicken cells (92%:7.7%:0.3%) and based on phosphoproteomics in human cells (84.1%:15.5%:0.4%) (Hunter and Sefton, 1980; Sharma et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Prophase I-arrested oocytes are distinct from other stages in that they display a limited number of phosphorylation sites at the relative maximum phosphorylation levels.
source: First, prophase I-arrested oocytes are distinct from those in the other stages in that they not only display a limited number of phosphorylation sites at the relative maximum phosphorylation levels (Figure 3C) but also have the lowest overall phosphorylation state of the samples tested (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: Prophase I-arrested oocytes have the lowest overall phosphorylation state of the samples tested.
source: First, prophase I-arrested oocytes are distinct from those in the other stages in that they not only display a limited number of phosphorylation sites at the relative maximum phosphorylation levels (Figure 3C) but also have the lowest overall phosphorylation state of the samples tested (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: More than half of the total phosphorylation sites identified were maximally phosphorylated in MI.
source: Second, more than half of the total phosphorylation sites identified were maximally phosphorylated in MI, whereas phosphorylation was substantially reduced in MII (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Phosphorylation was substantially reduced in MII compared to MI.
source: Second, more than half of the total phosphorylation sites identified were maximally phosphorylated in MI, whereas phosphorylation was substantially reduced in MII (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Patterns of phosphorylation imply a critical role for phosphoregulation in specializing the two meiotic and first cleavage divisions.
source: These patterns of phosphorylation imply a critical role for phosphoregulation in specializing the two meiotic and first cleavage divisions and suggest a role for a low phosphorylation state in maintaining the prophase I arrest.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the phosphoproteomic data patterns.

claim: A low phosphorylation state plays a role in maintaining the prophase I arrest.
source: These patterns of phosphorylation imply a critical role for phosphoregulation in specializing the two meiotic and first cleavage divisions and suggest a role for a low phosphorylation state in maintaining the prophase I arrest.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the phosphoproteomic data patterns.

claim: Inhibitory phosphorylation sites on Cdk1 or Cdk2 (Y21 or Y15, respectively) are phosphorylated in prophase I arrest, and to a lesser extent at first cleavage, but not during meiosis.
source: We first identified inhibitory phosphorylation sites on Cdk1 or Cdk2 (Y21 or Y15, respectively) by proteomics and western blotting using phospho-specific antibodies against these conserved sites (Figure 3E,F). These sites are phosphorylated in prophase I arrest, and to a lesser extent at first cleavage, but not during meiosis.
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data and western blotting shown in Figure 3E,F.

claim: Cdk is inactive in prophase I-arrested oocytes but active throughout the meiotic divisions.
source: This phosphorylation pattern suggests that Cdk is inactive in prophase I-arrested oocytes but active throughout the meiotic divisions.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the phosphorylation pattern of inhibitory sites on Cdk.

claim: A conserved activating phosphorylation on the MAP kinase p42/ERK phosphorylation (Y204) was undetectable in prophase I-arrested oocytes, high in MI and MII, and low in first cleavage.
source: Based on our phosphoproteomics and western blotting, we found that a conserved activating phosphorylation on the MAP kinase p42/ERK phosphorylation (Y204) was undetectable in prophase I-arrested oocytes, high in MI and MII, and low in first cleavage (Figure 3G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data and western blotting shown in Figure 3G,H.

claim: An increase in phosphorylation of the SGK activation segment was detected following hormonal stimulation.
source: In support of this model, we detected an increase in phosphorylation of the SGK activation segment following hormonal stimulation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: An increase in phosphorylation on Cdc25 S188, an activating SGK site, was observed following hormonal stimulation.
source: Concordantly, we observed an increase in phosphorylation on Cdc25 S188, an activating SGK site, and Myt1 S75, a repressive SGK site, following hormonal stimulation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B,C; Hiraoka et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B,C and cited prior work.

claim: An increase in phosphorylation on Myt1 S75, a repressive SGK site, was observed following hormonal stimulation.
source: Concordantly, we observed an increase in phosphorylation on Cdc25 S188, an activating SGK site, and Myt1 S75, a repressive SGK site, following hormonal stimulation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B,C; Hiraoka et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B,C and cited prior work.

claim: Sites that increased in phosphorylation abundance by more than threefold from prophase I to GVBD were enriched for a SGK-like consensus motif.
source: The sites that increased in abundance by more than threefold were enriched for a SGK-like consensus motif, whereas those that increased less displayed a more AKT-like motif (basophilic residues in the −4 position) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by motif analysis of phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Sites that increased in phosphorylation abundance by less than threefold from prophase I to GVBD displayed a more AKT-like motif.
source: The sites that increased in abundance by more than threefold were enriched for a SGK-like consensus motif, whereas those that increased less displayed a more AKT-like motif (basophilic residues in the −4 position) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by motif analysis of phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: SGK acts as the major trigger kinase driving meiotic resumption.
source: Collectively, these results support a model where SGK acts as the major trigger kinase driving meiotic resumption (Hiraoka et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data and cited prior work.

claim: A conserved activating phosphorylation within the activation segment of Greatwall kinase (T194 in humans; T204 in sea star) was identified.
source: We identified a conserved activating phosphorylation within the activation segment of Greatwall kinase (T194 in humans; T204 in sea star) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E; Blake-Hodek et al., 2012; Gharbi-Ayachi et al., 2010), indicative of high Greatwall kinase activity during GVBD and MI, and reduced activity in later stages.
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E and cited prior work.

claim: High Greatwall kinase activity occurs during GVBD and MI, and reduced activity in later stages.
source: We identified a conserved activating phosphorylation within the activation segment of Greatwall kinase (T194 in humans; T204 in sea star) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E; Blake-Hodek et al., 2012; Gharbi-Ayachi et al., 2010), indicative of high Greatwall kinase activity during GVBD and MI, and reduced activity in later stages.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the phosphorylation pattern of Greatwall kinase shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E.

claim: PP1 T316 (corresponding to T320 in humans) is hypo-phosphorylated in prophase I-arrested oocytes, which would result in high PP1 activity.
source: PP1 T316 (corresponding to T320 in humans) is hypo-phosphorylated in prophase I-arrested oocytes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2F), which would result in high PP1 activity.
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2F and knowledge of PP1 regulation.

claim: Analysis of the phosphorylation abundance of RVxF motifs across the phosphoproteomics time course revealed low RVxF phosphorylation occupancy in prophase I, which increased in GVBD and MI, before decreasing in later stages.
source: Analysis of the phosphorylation abundance of RVxF motifs across the phosphoproteomics time course revealed low RVxF phosphorylation occupancy in prophase I, which increased in GVBD and MI, before decreasing in later stages (Figure 3—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2G.

claim: In prophase I, the PP1 catalytic subunit is maximally bound to regulatory subunits to promote substrate dephosphorylation.
source: This suggests that, in prophase I, the PP1 catalytic subunit is maximally bound to regulatory subunits to promote substrate dephosphorylation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the low RVxF phosphorylation occupancy in prophase I.

claim: Phosphorylation adjacent to NIPP1's RVxF is low in prophase I-arrested oocytes, but increases following meiotic resumption.
source: Indeed, we found that phosphorylation adjacent to its RVxF is low in prophase I-arrested oocytes, but increases following meiotic resumption (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4A–C.

claim: Preventing NIPP1 phosphorylation with phospho-inhibitory mutations (P. miniata NIPP1 S199A or S197A S199A double mutants) resulted in a greater than fivefold increase in the binding of sea star NIPP1 to human PP1 when expressed in human 293T cells.
source: Preventing NIPP1 phosphorylation with phospho-inhibitory mutations (P. miniata NIPP1 S199A or S197A S199A double mutants) resulted in a greater than fivefold increase in the binding of sea star NIPP1 to human PP1 when expressed in human 293T cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 4D; Beullens et al., 1992; Beullens et al., 1999; Tanuma et al., 2008; Winkler et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4D and cited prior work.

claim: The low NIPP1 phosphorylation in prophase I oocytes would increase the association between PP1 and NIPP1, modulating and reducing its phosphatase activity toward specific substrates.
source: Thus, the low NIPP1 phosphorylation in prophase I oocytes would increase the association between PP1 and NIPP1, modulating and reducing its phosphatase activity toward specific substrates.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the phosphorylation data and binding experiments.

claim: PmARPP19 thio-phosphorylated in vitro by Greatwall kinase resulted in increased Cdc25 phosphorylation when added to mitotic human cell lysates.
source: Indeed, we found that PmARPP19 thio-phosphorylated in vitro by Greatwall kinase resulted in increased Cdc25 phosphorylation when added to mitotic human cell lysates (Figure 3—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro phosphatase assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5B.

claim: Phospho-ARPP19 S106 acts as an active B55 inhibitor such that ARPP19 phosphorylation serves as a proxy for assessing PP2A-B55 activity in sea star oocytes.
source: Thus, phospho-ARPP19 S106 acts as an active B55 inhibitor such that ARPP19 phosphorylation serves as a proxy for assessing PP2A-B55 activity in sea star oocytes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the in vitro assay and knowledge of ARPP19 function.

claim: PmARPP19 S106 phosphorylation is low in prophase I, but is high in GVBD and MI, before decreasing again in MII.
source: PmARPP19 S106 phosphorylation is low in prophase I, but is high in GVBD and MI, before decreasing again in MII (Figure 3—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5C.

claim: 100% of oocytes spontaneously underwent GVBD within 70 min following calyculin A addition.
source: Following calyculin A addition, we found that 100% of oocytes spontaneously underwent GVBD within 70 min (Figure 3—figure supplement 6A,C; also see Tosuji et al., 1991).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6A,C and cited prior work.

claim: Tautomycetin potently inhibited PP1 in in vitro phosphatase assays.
source: Using in vitro phosphatase assays, we confirmed that tautomycetin potently inhibited PP1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro phosphatase assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6B.

claim: Tautomycetin did not induce GVBD across a wide range of concentrations.
source: In contrast to calyculin A treatment, tautomycetin did not induce GVBD across a wide range of concentrations (Figure 3—figure supplement 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6C.

claim: Following meiotic resumption induced by hormonal stimulation, tautomycetin treatment caused meiotic chromosome alignment and segregation errors.
source: However, following meiotic resumption induced by hormonal stimulation, tautomycetin treatment did cause meiotic chromosome alignment and segregation errors (Figure 3—figure supplement 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6D.

claim: PP1 is dispensable for maintaining a prophase I arrest but is required to achieve high fidelity chromosome segregation during meiosis.
source: We therefore conclude that PP1 is dispensable for maintaining a prophase I arrest but is required to achieve high fidelity chromosome segregation during meiosis, with PP2A playing the critical role in maintaining the prophase I arrest.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the tautomycetin and calyculin A experiments.

claim: PP2A plays the critical role in maintaining the prophase I arrest.
source: We therefore conclude that PP1 is dispensable for maintaining a prophase I arrest but is required to achieve high fidelity chromosome segregation during meiosis, with PP2A playing the critical role in maintaining the prophase I arrest.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the tautomycetin and calyculin A experiments.

claim: Calyculin A treatment revealed a broad upregulation of phosphorylation, with 85% of phosphorylation sites displaying a high level of phosphorylation after 70 min of calyculin A treatment.
source: This analysis revealed a broad upregulation of phosphorylation (Supplementary file 5), with 85% of phosphorylation sites displaying a high level of phosphorylation after 70 min of calyculin A treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 7A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 7A,B and supplementary file 5.

claim: Phosphorylation sites with a normal maximal phosphorylation occupancy in prophase I decreased after 70 min of calyculin A treatment.
source: However, phosphorylation sites with a normal maximal phosphorylation occupancy in prophase I (when PP2A displays high activity) decreased after 70 min of calyculin A treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 7B).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 7B.

claim: Although global phosphorylation levels increased similarly to those observed upon meiotic entry, calyculin A-treated oocytes failed to progress past a GVBD-like state.
source: Although global phosphorylation levels increased similarly to those observed upon meiotic entry, calyculin A-treated oocytes failed to progress past this GVBD-like state based on the absence of a contractile actin network, chromosome congression, or spindle formation (Figure 3—figure supplement 7C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 7C.

claim: PP2A phosphatase activity is required to maintain a normal prophase I arrest, but its inhibition is not sufficient to recapitulate physiological meiotic resumption.
source: Therefore, although PP2A phosphatase activity is required to maintain a normal prophase I arrest, its inhibition is not sufficient to recapitulate physiological meiotic resumption.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the calyculin A experiments.

claim: MI displayed the largest number of sites with maximal phosphorylation among the stages tested.
source: Of the stages tested, MI displayed the largest number of sites with maximal phosphorylation (Figure 3A), including a large number of sites with a TP or SP consensus motif indicative of CDK- or MAPK-dependent phosphorylation (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3A and supplementary file 5.

claim: MI includes a large number of sites with a TP or SP consensus motif indicative of CDK- or MAPK-dependent phosphorylation.
source: Of the stages tested, MI displayed the largest number of sites with maximal phosphorylation (Figure 3A), including a large number of sites with a TP or SP consensus motif indicative of CDK- or MAPK-dependent phosphorylation (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data in supplementary file 5 and knowledge of kinase consensus motifs.

claim: Phosphorylation of MI sites increased when oocytes were treated with calyculin A, indicating that they are putative substrates for PP1 or PP2A.
source: Moreover, phosphorylation of these sites increased when oocytes were treated with the calyculin A, indicating that they are putative substrates for PP1 or PP2A (Figure 3—figure supplement 7A,B, supplementary file 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 7A,B and supplementary file 5.

claim: Hierarchical clustering of peptides with a single phosphorylation site maximally phosphorylated in MI revealed three distinct clusters.
source: Hierarchical clustering of peptides with a single phosphorylation site maximally phosphorylated in MI revealed three distinct clusters (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: A subset of sites sharply decreased in their phosphorylation after MI (cluster 3).
source: A subset of sites sharply decreased in their phosphorylation after MI (Figure 4B, cluster 3), whereas other sites remained phosphorylated during MII and the first embryonic cleavage (Figure 4B, cluster 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Other sites remained phosphorylated during MII and the first embryonic cleavage (cluster 2).
source: A subset of sites sharply decreased in their phosphorylation after MI (Figure 4B, cluster 3), whereas other sites remained phosphorylated during MII and the first embryonic cleavage (Figure 4B, cluster 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: A third cluster displayed intermediate dephosphorylation kinetics (cluster 1).
source: A third cluster displayed intermediate dephosphorylation kinetics (Figure 4B, cluster 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Differential phosphorylation behaviors could provide a mechanism by which the meiotic divisions are specified and underlie the transition from MI to MII.
source: These differential behaviors could provide a mechanism by which the meiotic divisions are specified and underlie the transition from MI to MII.
evidence: The claim is a speculative inference from the differential phosphorylation behaviors.

claim: Motif analysis of single phosphorylation sites in cluster 3 revealed that they predominantly occur on threonine with proline in the +1 position (TP sites).
source: Motif analysis of single phosphorylation sites in cluster 3 revealed that they predominantly occur on threonine with proline in the +1 position (TP sites).
evidence: The claim is supported by motif analysis of phosphoproteomic data.

claim: By directly comparing the phosphorylation of SP vs TP sites in the three clusters, TP phosphorylation declined more substantially than SP after MI.
source: Indeed, by directly comparing the phosphorylation of SP vs TP sites in the three clusters, we found that TP phosphorylation declined more substantially than SP after MI (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: On average, the mean phosphorylation of TP motifs detected by phosphoproteomics peaked in MI, but then declined substantially in MII.
source: On average, the mean phosphorylation of TP motifs detected by phosphoproteomics peaked in MI, but then declined substantially in MII.
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data.

claim: SP motif phosphorylation decreased to a lesser extent than TP motif phosphorylation.
source: In contrast, SP motif phosphorylation decreased to a lesser extent (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: TP phosphorylation is lower on average in prophase I-arrested oocytes compared to SP phosphorylation.
source: To evaluate differential SP vs TP phosphorylation at other cell cycle stages, we additionally analyzed their relative abundances in prophase I-arrested oocytes and found that TP phosphorylation is lower on average (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Overall TP site phosphorylation peaked in MI, followed by strong reduction in MII, as confirmed by western blots using antibodies against phosphorylated pTP and pSP CDK motifs.
source: Consistent with our MS results, overall TP site phosphorylation peaked in MI, followed by strong reduction in MII. In contrast, SP phosphorylation declined less substantially at the MI/MII transition (Figure 4G, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: SP phosphorylation declined less substantially at the MI/MII transition compared to TP phosphorylation, as confirmed by western blots.
source: Consistent with our MS results, overall TP site phosphorylation peaked in MI, followed by strong reduction in MII. In contrast, SP phosphorylation declined less substantially at the MI/MII transition (Figure 4G, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The same trends of differential TP vs SP dephosphorylation were observed with antibodies recognizing TPP and SPP phosphorylation motifs.
source: The same trends were observed with antibodies recognizing TPP and SPP phosphorylation motifs (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Despite the transient inactivation of Cdk1 between the meiotic divisions, SP phosphorylation remains relatively stable during this window.
source: Thus, despite the transient inactivation of Cdk1 between the meiotic divisions (Okano-Uchida et al., 1998), SP phosphorylation remains relatively stable during this window.
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data and cited prior work.

claim: MAPK activity remains high between both meiotic divisions.
source: We note that MAPK activity remains high between both meiotic divisions (Figure 3G,H) and could contribute to the relative stability of SP phosphorylation events during this window.
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic and western blot data shown in Figure 3G,H.

claim: A phosphatase activity is required to preferentially oppose TP phosphorylation sites to account for the difference in SP vs TP behavior.
source: However, this model would still require a phosphatase activity to preferentially oppose TP phosphorylation sites to account for the difference in SP vs TP behavior.
evidence: The claim is a logical inference from the differential behavior of SP vs TP sites.

claim: The identity of surrounding residues correlated with phosphorylation behavior, with an enrichment for basic amino acids starting in the +2 position and a depletion of acidic amino acids.
source: In addition to differences in the phosphorylated residue (T vs S), we also found that the identity of surrounding residues correlated with phosphorylation behavior. Specifically, we identified an enrichment for basic amino acids starting in the +2 position (e.g., lysine) and a depletion of acidic amino acids (e.g., aspartic and glutamic acid) (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by motif analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: TP sites with a small non-polar (A or G) or basic (K or R) amino acid were significantly more dephosphorylated than TP with acidic amino acids (E or D) or proline.
source: For example, TP sites with a small non-polar (A or G) or basic (K or R) amino acid were significantly more dephosphorylated than TP with acidic amino acids (E or D) or proline (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The sites preferentially dephosphorylated at the MI/MII transition (cluster 3, TP followed by basic or nonpolar amino acids) match the sequence preferences of the phosphatase PP2A-B55.
source: Importantly, we note that the sites preferentially dephosphorylated at the MI/MII transition (cluster 3, TP followed by basic or nonpolar amino acids) match the sequence preferences of the phosphatase PP2A-B55, which we and others have recently reported (Cundell et al., 2016; Holder et al., 2020; Kruse et al., 2020; McCloy et al., 2015; Touati et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by motif analysis and cited prior work on PP2A-B55 substrate preferences.

claim: PP2A-B55 drives the striking difference in behavior between TP and SP sites at the MI/MII transition.
source: These observations raise the possibility that PP2A-B55 drives the striking difference in behavior between TP and SP sites at the MI/MII transition.
evidence: The claim is a speculative inference from the motif analysis and PP2A-B55 substrate preferences.

claim: Following MI, the dataset reveals a decrease in cyclin B levels and a corresponding reduction in the activating phosphorylation on Greatwall kinase (T204) and ARPP19 (S106).
source: Indeed, following MI, our dataset reveals a decrease in cyclin B levels and a corresponding reduction in the activating phosphorylation on Greatwall kinase (T204) and ARPP19 (S106).
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic and phosphoproteomic data.

claim: The decrease in cyclin B levels and reduction in Greatwall and ARPP19 phosphorylation would result in the release of PP2A-B55 to dephosphorylate its substrates at the MI/MII transition.
source: This would result in the release of PP2A-B55 to dephosphorylate its substrates at the MI/MII transition (Figure 5B, Figure 3—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the phosphorylation patterns of regulatory factors.

claim: PP2A-B55 is reactivated at the MI/MII transition to preferentially dephosphorylate specific substrates with TP/basic consensus motifs, through a conserved pathway involving ARPP19, Greatwall, and CDK/cyclin B.
source: Together, these observations suggest that PP2A-B55 is reactivated at the MI/MII transition to preferentially dephosphorylate specific substrates with TP/basic consensus motifs, through a conserved pathway involving ARPP19, Greatwall, and CDK/cyclin B (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the phosphorylation patterns and regulatory pathway analysis.

claim: Phosphorylation sites that decrease in abundance between MI and MII samples in Xenopus oocytes were enriched for TP-basic sequences but depleted for SP-acidic sequences.
source: Strikingly, we found that the phosphorylation sites that decrease in abundance between these samples in Xenopus oocytes were also enriched for TP-basic sequences but depleted for SP-acidic sequences (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by reanalysis of published Xenopus phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The differential behavior of SP and TP phosphorylation may represent a conserved regulatory mechanism for meiosis in animals.
source: Thus, based on this cross-species comparison, the differential behavior of SP and TP phosphorylation may represent a conserved regulatory mechanism for meiosis in animals and suggests that PP2A-B55 is an important conductor of the MI/MII transition.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the cross-species comparison of phosphoproteomic data.

claim: PP2A-B55 is an important conductor of the MI/MII transition.
source: Thus, based on this cross-species comparison, the differential behavior of SP and TP phosphorylation may represent a conserved regulatory mechanism for meiosis in animals and suggests that PP2A-B55 is an important conductor of the MI/MII transition.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the cross-species comparison and motif analysis.

claim: Ectopic expression of the B55 alanine mutant (DE/A) induced spontaneous GVBD and apoptosis in prophase I-arrested oocytes.
source: Compared to wild-type B55, ectopic expression of the alanine mutant (DE/A) induced spontaneous GVBD and apoptosis in prophase I-arrested oocytes (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: PP2A is specifically required to maintain the prophase I arrest.
source: This result, along with the effect that we observed following calyculin A treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 6A,C), further supports our model in which PP2A is specifically required to maintain the prophase I arrest.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the B55 mutant and calyculin A experiments.

claim: Oocytes expressing the B55 alanine mutant (DE/A) successfully assembled the MI spindle and completed cytokinesis of polar body I, but MII spindles failed to form properly and displayed a ball-like morphology.
source: Oocytes expressing the alanine mutant (DE/A) successfully assembled the MI spindle and completed cytokinesis of polar body I. However, events after MI did not occur, with the MII spindles failing to form properly and displaying a ball-like morphology.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data.

claim: Anaphase and cytokinesis did not progress normally in B55 DE/A mutant oocytes, resulting in a reduced rate of polar body II extrusion.
source: Furthermore, anaphase and cytokinesis did not progress normally, resulting in a reduced rate of polar body II extrusion (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: Oocytes expressing the B55 charge-swap mutations (DE/K) displayed a more severe phenotype: the first meiotic spindle formed normally, but remained arrested, with the bivalent chromosomes maintaining cohesion and the co-oriented centromeres remaining fused.
source: Oocytes expressing the charge-swap mutations (DE/K) displayed a more severe phenotype: the first meiotic spindle formed normally, but remained arrested, with the bivalent chromosomes maintaining cohesion and the co-oriented centromeres remaining fused, even at time points where wild-type control oocytes completed MII.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data.

claim: Although normal anaphase I and cytokinesis did not occur in B55 DE/K mutant oocytes, the spindle poles eventually separated, ultimately resulting in two semi-distinct spindles.
source: However, although normal anaphase I and cytokinesis did not occur, the spindle poles eventually separated, ultimately resulting in two semi-distinct spindles.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data.

claim: Pole fragmentation in B55 DE/K mutant oocytes was due to the separation of the pair of centrioles in the spindle pole.
source: Staining for Centrin2 revealed that pole fragmentation was due to the separation of the pair of centrioles in the spindle pole (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is supported by Centrin2 staining data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Alterations to PP2A-B55 substrate specificity allow MI events to occur, but prevent changes to the cell division machinery that occur at the MI/MII transition.
source: Therefore, alterations to PP2A-B55 substrate specificity allow MI events to occur, but prevent changes to the cell division machinery that occur at the MI/MII transition.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the B55 mutant experiments.

claim: PP2A-B55 serves as an essential regulator of the MI/MII transition by selectively dephosphorylating substrates to achieve exit from MI, but retaining sites that must remain phosphorylated for MII to occur.
source: We, therefore, propose that PP2A-B55 serves as an essential regulator of the MI/MII transition by selectively dephosphorylating substrates to achieve exit from MI, but retaining sites that must remain phosphorylated for MII to occur.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model inferred from the B55 mutant experiments.

claim: Conserved phosphorylation sites on PRC1 (T470 in humans, T411 in sea star), TPX2 (T369 in humans, T508 in sea star), and INCENP (T59 in humans, T61 in sea star) are known substrates of PP2A-B55.
source: We identified several conserved phosphorylation sites on PRC1 (T470 in humans, T411 in sea star), TPX2 (T369 in humans, T508 in sea star), and Inner Centromere Protein (INCENP) (T59 in humans, T61 in sea star) (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A–C) that are known substrates of PP2A-B55 (Cundell et al., 2016; Hein et al., 2017; Hümmer and Mayer, 2009; Jiang et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3A–C and cited prior work.

claim: Consistent with the reactivation of PP2A-B55, PRC1, TPX2, and INCENP substrates display a stark decrease in phosphorylation following MI.
source: Consistent with the reactivation of PP2A-B55, these substrates display a stark decrease in phosphorylation following MI.
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data.

claim: An SP phosphorylation event on Prc1 (S571) remains relatively constant during the meiotic divisions.
source: In contrast to the behavior of these conserved PP2A-B55 substrate sites, we identified an SP phosphorylation event on Prc1 (S571), whose levels remain relatively constant during the meiotic divisions (Figure 5—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3D.

claim: Relative to other TP sites, an SP phosphorylation in Tpx2 (S625) was dephosphorylated to a lesser degree following MI.
source: Furthermore, relative to other TP sites, an SP phosphorylation in Tpx2 (S625) was dephosphorylated to a lesser degree following MI (Figure 5—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3E.

claim: INCENP-GFP localized to centromeres in metaphase of MI, but then translocated to the central spindle at anaphase of MI.
source: Using a green fluorescent protein (GFP) fusion construct, we found that INCENP-GFP localized to centromeres in metaphase of MI, but then translocated to the central spindle at anaphase of MI.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data.

claim: In MII, INCENP localization to centromeres was reduced, but it then returned at the midzone in anaphase II.
source: In MII, INCENP localization to centromeres was reduced, but it then returned at the midzone in anaphase II.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data.

claim: As the maternal pronucleus formed at meiotic exit, INCENP localized to nucleolar structures.
source: As the maternal pronucleus formed at meiotic exit, INCENP localized to nucleolar structures (Figure 5—figure supplement 3F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3F.

claim: Expression of the B55 DE/A mutant significantly reduced translocation of INCENP to the central spindle in anaphase of MI.
source: In contrast, expression of the B55 DE/A mutant significantly reduced translocation of INCENP to the central spindle (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6B,C.

claim: The selective activity of PP2A-B55 is required for the proper localization behavior of INCENP at the MI/MII transition.
source: Therefore, the selective activity of PP2A-B55 is required for the proper localization behavior of INCENP at the MI/MII transition.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the B55 mutant experiments.

claim: Phosphorylation on INCENP T61 sharply decreased following MI, whereas other proline-directed sites on INCENP remained phosphorylated throughout the oocyte-to-embryo transition.
source: Consistent with this model, we found that phosphorylation on INCENP T61 sharply decreased following MI, whereas other proline-directed sites on INCENP remained phosphorylated throughout the oocyte-to-embryo transition (Figure 6A, Figure 5—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 5—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Sequence alignment of sea star T61 with human INCENP T59 revealed the presence of a conserved downstream basic patch, supporting its potentially conserved dephosphorylation by PP2A-B55.
source: Sequence alignment of sea star T61 with human INCENP T59 revealed the presence of a conserved downstream basic patch, supporting its potentially conserved dephosphorylation by PP2A-B55 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence alignment shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3C and knowledge of PP2A-B55 substrate preferences.

claim: INCENP T506 remains relatively stable, likely due to the presence of downstream acidic amino acids, thereby disfavoring PP2A-B55 association.
source: In contrast, T506 remains relatively stable, likely due to the presence of downstream acidic amino acids, thereby disfavoring PP2A-B55 association (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the phosphorylation pattern and knowledge of PP2A-B55 substrate preferences.

claim: INCENP(T61S)-GFP failed to translocate to the central spindle in anaphase of MI and remained at high levels at centromeres.
source: In contrast, INCENP(T61S)-GFP failed to translocate to the central spindle in anaphase of MI and remained at high levels at centromeres (Figure 6D,E), consistent with prior work in mitosis (Goto et al., 2006; Hümmer and Mayer, 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6D,E and cited prior work.

claim: The retention of INCENP at centromeres in anaphase I suggests that the T61 residue remains phosphorylated at the MI/MII transition when substituted with serine, a lower affinity substrate for PP2A-B55.
source: The retention of INCENP at centromeres in anaphase I suggests that this residue remains phosphorylated at the MI/MII transition when substituted with serine, a lower affinity substrate for PP2A-B55.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the INCENP T61S mutant experiments and knowledge of PP2A-B55 substrate preferences.

claim: The usage of serine vs threonine, modulated by adjacent charged amino acids, can directly encode a differential response to a common set of kinases and phosphatases, enabling rewiring events at key cell cycle transitions.
source: Thus, the usage of serine vs threonine, modulated by adjacent charged amino acids, can directly encode a differential response to a common set of kinases and phosphatases, enabling rewiring events at key cell cycle transitions.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model inferred from the INCENP experiments and phosphoproteomic data.

claim: Through the paradigm of differential S vs T phosphorylation, the behaviors of individual proteins may be temporally coordinated with meiotic cell cycle progression to achieve specific behaviors.
source: Through this paradigm, the behaviors of individual proteins may be temporally coordinated with meiotic cell cycle progression to achieve specific behaviors.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model inferred from the experimental data.

claim: Overall protein levels are stable but selected cell cycle regulators, including cyclins A and B, must undergo new protein synthesis for progression through meiosis.
source: Using TMT-based proteomics, phosphoproteomics, and functional approaches, we found that overall protein levels are stable but that selected cell cycle regulators, including cyclins A and B, must undergo new protein synthesis for progression through meiosis.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the proteomic and morpholino experiments.

claim: The general stability of the proteome across the oocyte-to-embryo transition in sea stars is consistent with prior results in oocytes of the vertebrate X. laevis.
source: This general stability of the proteome across the oocyte-to-embryo transition in sea stars is consistent with prior results in oocytes of the vertebrate X. laevis (Peuchen et al., 2017; Presler et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison to cited prior work.

claim: Post-translational modification serves as the primary and conserved control mechanism for meiosis and the transition to early development.
source: Therefore, post-translational modification instead serves as the primary and conserved control mechanism for meiosis and the transition to early development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the proteomic data and comparison to prior work.

claim: The prophase I arrest is characterized by low overall phosphorylation and maintaining this arrest requires phosphatase activity.
source: We found that the prophase I arrest is characterized by low overall phosphorylation and that maintaining this arrest requires phosphatase activity.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the phosphoproteomic and calyculin A experiments.

claim: Although serine and threonine residues are often considered as conserved and interchangeable, distinct behaviors for TP and SP phosphorylation were observed at the MI/MII transition, with threonine sites being preferentially dephosphorylated.
source: Strikingly, although serine and threonine residues are often considered as conserved and interchangeable, we observed distinct behaviors for TP and SP phosphorylation at the MI/MII transition, with threonine sites being preferentially dephosphorylated.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the phosphoproteomic data.

claim: Differential dephosphorylation suggests a novel paradigm for the regulatory control of oocytes, which must rapidly transition between the two meiotic divisions for the specialized meiotic cell cycle.
source: Such differential dephosphorylation suggests a novel paradigm for the regulatory control of oocytes, which must rapidly transition between the two meiotic divisions for the specialized meiotic cell cycle.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model inferred from the phosphoproteomic data.

claim: Upon the decrease in Cdk activity at the MI/MII transition, selective dephosphorylation of TP vs SP sites by PP2A-B55 is essential for meiotic progression.
source: Our analysis reveals that, upon the decrease in Cdk activity at the MI/MII transition, selective dephosphorylation of TP vs SP sites by PP2A-B55 is essential for meiotic progression.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the phosphoproteomic and B55 mutant experiments.

claim: Preferential TP dephosphorylation has been previously reported to create a temporal order to the cellular events during mitotic exit.
source: Preferential TP dephosphorylation has been previously reported to create a temporal order to the cellular events during mitotic exit (Cundell et al., 2016; Hein et al., 2017; McCloy et al., 2015; Touati et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In addition to temporal regulation of dephosphorylation at mitotic exit, preferential dephosphorylation of TP motifs could provide a mechanism to specify the two meiotic divisions in oocytes.
source: However, our work suggests that, in addition to temporal regulation of dephosphorylation at mitotic exit, preferential dephosphorylation of these motifs could provide a mechanism to specify the two meiotic divisions in oocytes.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model inferred from the experimental data.

claim: Threonine and serine phosphorylation is not interchangeable but instead represents an important regulatory mechanism to temporally control cellular processes.
source: Our work supports the emerging picture that threonine and serine phosphorylation is not interchangeable (Cundell et al., 2016; Deana et al., 1982; Deana and Pinna, 1988; Hein et al., 2017; Pinna et al., 1976) but instead represents an important regulatory mechanism to temporally control cellular processes.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data and cited prior work.

claim: In cultured mitotic cells, threonine dephosphorylation is important for timely mitotic exit.
source: In cultured mitotic cells, threonine dephosphorylation is important for timely mitotic exit.
evidence: The claim is supported by knowledge from prior work.

claim: Inhibitory phosphorylations on the APC/C regulator Cdc20 are conserved as threonines, whereas serine substitution mutants display delayed dephosphorylation and delayed Cdc20 activation.
source: For example, inhibitory phosphorylations on the APC/C regulator Cdc20 are conserved as threonines, whereas serine substitution mutants display delayed dephosphorylation and delayed Cdc20 activation (Hein et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Differential dephosphorylation provides not just a kinetic delay but also confers distinct behaviors for the two different meiotic divisions.
source: Our work extends this model into a new physiological context, wherein differential dephosphorylation provides not just a kinetic delay but also confers distinct behaviors for the two different meiotic divisions.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model inferred from the experimental data.

claim: Substitution of threonine 61 for serine on INCENP, which is subject to inhibitory phosphorylation by Cdk1, resulted in its failure to translocate to the central spindle in anaphase of MI.
source: For example, in our mutant analysis, substitution of threonine 61 for serine on INCENP, which is subject to inhibitory phosphorylation by Cdk1, resulted in its failure to translocate to the central spindle in anaphase of MI.
evidence: The claim is supported by the INCENP T61S mutant experiments.

claim: This phosphorylation code is further modulated by the charge of adjacent amino acids, with positively charged residues favoring PP2A-B55 association.
source: This phosphorylation code is further modulated by the charge of adjacent amino acids, with positively charged residues favoring PP2A-B55 association.
evidence: The claim is supported by motif analysis and knowledge of PP2A-B55 substrate preferences.

claim: Differential dephosphorylation represents a novel paradigm for the regulatory control of oocytes, which must rapidly transition between the two meiotic divisions for the specialized meiotic cell cycle.
source: Such differential dephosphorylation represents a novel paradigm for the regulatory control of oocytes, which must rapidly transition between the two meiotic divisions for the specialized meiotic cell cycle.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model inferred from the experimental data.

claim: PP2A-B55 is a critical conductor of cell cycle progression in oocytes.
source: These results point to PP2A-B55 as a critical conductor of cell cycle progression in oocytes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data.

claim: In diverse species, ARPP19/ENSA is required for exit from prophase I arrest in response to hormonal stimulation by inhibiting PP2A-B55.
source: In diverse species, ARPP19/ENSA is required for exit from prophase I arrest in response to hormonal stimulation by inhibiting PP2A-B55 (Dupré et al., 2013; Dupré et al., 2014; Matthews and Evans, 2014; Okumura et al., 2014; Von Stetina et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Although there is considerable conservation among the downstream phosphorylation steps associated with Cdk1 activation and meiotic progression, the upstream triggers of meiotic cell cycle resumption have diverged across evolution.
source: Intriguingly, although there is considerable conservation among the downstream phosphorylation steps associated with Cdk1 activation and meiotic progression, the upstream triggers of meiotic cell cycle resumption have diverged across evolution.
evidence: The claim is supported by knowledge from prior work.

claim: Numerous species, including mammals, sea stars, and cnidarians (jellyfish), all utilize GPCRs that respond to hormonal signals and undergo communication with surrounding somatic ovarian cells to propagate signals.
source: For example, numerous species, including mammals, sea stars, and cnidarians (jellyfish), all utilize GPCRs that respond to hormonal signals and undergo communication with surrounding somatic ovarian cells to propagate signals (Jaffe and Norris, 2010; Quiroga Artigas et al., 2020; Tadenuma et al., 1992).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The hormone/receptor pairs differ amongst species.
source: However, the hormone/receptor pairs differ amongst species.
evidence: The claim is supported by knowledge from prior work.

claim: In mice, luteinizing hormone acts upon receptors expressed in somatic cells and induces them to reduce the production of cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) and close gap-junction connections with the oocytes, leading to a decrease in cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) levels in the oocyte, a drop in protein kinase A (PKA) activity, and the subsequent release from meiotic arrest by activation of Cdc25.
source: In mice, luteinizing hormone acts upon receptors expressed in somatic cells and induces them to reduce the production of cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) and close gap-junction connections with the oocytes. This leads to a decrease in cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) levels in the oocyte, a drop in protein kinase A (PKA) activity, and the subsequent release from meiotic arrest by activation of Cdc25 (Conti and Chang, 2016; Norris et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In X. laevis, a drop in PKA activity is associated with meiotic resumption downstream of progesterone stimulation, although the nature of the roles of PKA and cAMP is disputed.
source: Similarly, in X. laevis, a drop in PKA activity is associated with meiotic resumption downstream of progesterone stimulation, although the nature of the roles of PKA and cAMP is disputed (Dupré et al., 2014; Nader et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In echinoderms, meiotic resumption is stimulated by the hormone 1-MeAd, which is synthesized by surrounding somatic cells and acts upon an unidentified GPCR, leading to the activation of the trigger kinase SGK.
source: In echinoderms, meiotic resumption is stimulated by the hormone 1-MeAd, which is synthesized by surrounding somatic cells and acts upon an unidentified GPCR, leading to the activation of the trigger kinase SGK (Kishimoto, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Although upstream steps of meiotic resumption are divergent, they still result in the downstream activation of Cdc25 and inhibition of Myt1, as in vertebrate oocyte systems.
source: Although these upstream steps are divergent, they still result in the downstream activation of Cdc25 and inhibition of Myt1, as in vertebrate oocyte systems.
evidence: The claim is supported by knowledge from prior work.

claim: Data from sea stars indicate that phosphatase activity is critical not only for maintaining the prophase I arrest but also to drive the transition between the two meiotic divisions.
source: Our data from sea stars indicate that phosphatase activity is critical not only for maintaining the prophase I arrest but also to drive the transition between the two meiotic divisions.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the experimental data.

claim: Prior work in mouse oocytes found that the Greatwall ortholog Mastl is essential to proceed past MI.
source: In support of a potentially conserved role for PP2A-B55 in the MI/MII transition, prior work in mouse oocytes found that the Greatwall ortholog Mastl is essential to proceed past MI (Adhikari et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: CDK and MAPK, combined with a wave of opposing PP2A-B55 activity at the MI/MII transition, provide a pacemaker for meiotic cell cycle progression.
source: CDK and MAPK, combined with a wave of opposing PP2A-B55 activity at the MI/MII transition, provide a pacemaker for meiotic cell cycle progression.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model inferred from the experimental data.

claim: By encoding PP2A-B55 affinity into substrates, different temporal phosphorylation profiles can be achieved yielding subsets of cell division proteins that are constitutively active but others that are uniquely modified in MI or MII.
source: By encoding PP2A-B55 affinity into substrates, different temporal phosphorylation profiles can be achieved yielding subsets of cell division proteins that are constitutively active but others that are uniquely modified in MI or MII.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model inferred from the experimental data.

claim: The rapidity of the two meiotic divisions (separated by only 30 min in sea stars) places a selective pressure for specific substrates to be promptly dephosphorylated.
source: The rapidity of the two meiotic divisions (separated by only 30 min in sea stars) places a selective pressure for specific substrates to be promptly dephosphorylated.
evidence: The claim is a speculative inference from the experimental data.

claim: Other sites may need to remain phosphorylated to prevent exit into interphase, creating evolutionary pressure for conservation as serine.
source: In contrast, other sites may need to remain phosphorylated to prevent exit into interphase, creating evolutionary pressure for conservation as serine.
evidence: The claim is a speculative inference from the experimental data.

claim: Evolution has fine-tuned substrate dephosphorylation by selecting for amino acid sequences that favor or disfavor the interaction with PP2A-B55, thereby enabling precise temporal coordination of events in the oocyte-to-embryo transition.
source: We propose that evolution has fine-tuned substrate dephosphorylation by selecting for amino acid sequences that favor or disfavor the interaction with PP2A-B55, thereby enabling precise temporal coordination of events in the oocyte-to-embryo transition.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model inferred from the experimental data.
